verdict.rationale: Azure documents a public REST API at management.azure.com, with per-operation reference pages and a Try It console, a documented api-version convention, Entra ID client registration for securing requests, and client libraries for most services. Machine-readable specs are published in the canonical Azure/azure-rest-api-specs repo, and a lifecycle policy commits to 12 months' notice before retiring REST APIs. The probe 404s on learn.microsoft.com OpenAPI paths do not contradict this, because the specs live in GitHub. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of driving the REST API end-to-end, and specs at a standard discoverable path (they are Swagger 2.0 or TypeSpec-generated with shifting folder layout).
